claims.text: Multi-scale modeling-based optimization can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in metallic materials.
Multi-scale modeling can identify microstructural configurations that balance strength and ductility.
The proposed intervention transforms a conventional microstructure into an optimized microstructure.
Computational modeling identifies optimal grain size and grain-size distribution.
Computational modeling identifies optimal precipitation characteristics and defect density.
The proposed optimization produces a 20% increase in strength relative to conventional processing.
The proposed optimization produces a 15% increase in ductility relative to conventional processing.
The hypothesis applies to metallic materials with conventional microstructures under ambient conditions and typical loading rates.
The effectiveness of the approach is limited by computational-model accuracy and the availability of experimental validation data.
